title: U.S. House · Texas's 9th District
area: A redrawn district covering the Houston Ship Channel area and Liberty County, east and southeast of Houston.

context.text: Open seat. Texas redrew its congressional map in August 2025, and the redrawn 9th District became substantially more Republican-leaning than the district previously represented by Democratic incumbent Al Green. Rather than run for re-election here, Green ran against fellow Democratic incumbent Christian Menefee in the redrawn, safely Democratic 18th District, and lost the May 26, 2026 primary runoff. Leticia Gutierrez won the Democratic primary for the open 9th District seat; Alex Mealer won a Republican primary runoff over Briscoe Cain.

candidates.name: Leticia Gutierrez
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary in a multi-candidate field

summary.text: Leticia Gutierrez is the Democratic nominee for the open U.S. House seat in Texas's 9th District. A government relations and community outreach director with a finance degree from the University of St. Thomas, she describes a long career connecting working families with elected officials and agencies, with a focus on children's health. She won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary and is running on affordability and infrastructure resilience.

background.text: According to her campaign website, her parents were farm laborers and she has called the district home for 45 years; she attended Milby High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of St. Thomas; her Candidate Connection survey lists it as Finance and Economics.

Ballotpedia lists her profession as a government relations and community outreach director; her campaign website says she works with elected officials and government agencies on behalf of her community.
Says she has advocated for children's health for years after her son developed asthma as a child, and describes herself as a single mother of two whose oldest son serves in the U.S. Army.
Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for the redrawn 9th District in a multi-candidate field.

priorities.text: Everyday affordability: says rising costs of groceries and other necessities are forcing families to forgo healthcare and housing investments.
Making government work for constituents, including ending what she describes as subsidies to large corporations paid for by working families.
Infrastructure resilience: cites Hurricane Harvey, Winter Storm Uri and the derecho as reasons to invest in aging pipes, power lines and roads.

positions.summary: Says the government has been giving subsidies to large corporations while working families 'foot the bill,' and wants that to end.

candidates.researchNotes: Gutierrez's employer and any prior public offices are not named in the sources reviewed; the biography relies on her campaign website and Ballotpedia.

candidates.name: Alex Mealer
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 26, 2026 Republican primary runoff over Briscoe Cain

summary.text: Alex Mealer is the Republican nominee for the open U.S. House seat in Texas's 9th District. A West Point graduate, Army explosive ordnance disposal officer and Harvard-trained lawyer, she worked in energy-sector finance, ran for Harris County Judge in 2022, and served on the METRO board. She won the May 26, 2026 Republican runoff over Briscoe Cain and is running on border security, public safety and the Houston Ship Channel economy.

background.text: Graduated from the United States Military Academy at West Point in 2007 and served as an Explosive Ordnance Disposal officer in the U.S. Army, including combat service in Afghanistan, according to her campaign website.
Earned an MBA and a J.D. from Harvard University in 2016; her campaign website says she was a member of the Federalist Society and the Adam Smith Society there.

Moved to Houston to work in energy finance, advising public and private companies on mergers and acquisitions and capital-markets financing; Ballotpedia describes her as an oil and gas finance executive.
Owns a welding supply company with her husband, Clay, according to Ballotpedia; her campaign website describes her as a small business owner.

Ran for Harris County Judge in 2022 as a first-time candidate, winning a nine-candidate Republican primary (per her campaign website) and losing the general election to incumbent Lina Hidalgo, 49.2% to 50.8%.
Served as Public Safety Chair on the Metropolitan Transit Authority of Harris County (METRO) board from 2024 to 2025.
Won the May 26, 2026 Republican primary runoff over Briscoe Cain, 68.3% to 31.7%.
According to her campaign website, she and her husband Clay, also a West Point graduate, have two children and attend Second Baptist.

priorities.text: Border security and immigration enforcement, framed as part of a broader 'America First' agenda.
Public safety: says law enforcement should be fully resourced and equipped to protect communities.
Protecting the Houston Ship Channel and port economy, which she says generates more than $1 trillion in GDP for the region.

positions.summary: Lists keeping the border secure as the first item of her platform to pass what she calls President Trump's 'America First Agenda.'
Says she is committed to ensuring law enforcement is 'fully resourced' with the tools needed to protect communities.

candidates.researchNotes: Mealer's biography draws on her campaign website and Ballotpedia; the account of the 2022 election contest on her website is her own description and is not summarized here.
